title: Quantum superposition & measurement (SAMPLE)

pre.prompt: A qubit in state (|0⟩ + |1⟩)/√2 is measured in the computational (|0⟩/|1⟩) basis many times, one shot per copy. What best describes the individual outcomes and their long-run frequencies?
options: Each run is individually unpredictable, and the frequencies converge to about half 0 and half 1.
The first run is random, but every later run repeats the first outcome.
The outcomes alternate strictly between 0 and 1.
Every run returns 0 because both amplitudes are positive.
pre.explanation: Born rule: equal amplitudes mean equal probabilities per shot; single runs are random, frequencies stabilize over many shots.

post.prompt: TRANSFER: many ions are prepared identically with spin pointing along +x, i.e. the state (|↑z⟩ + |↓z⟩)/√2. A Stern–Gerlach magnet oriented along the SAME x axis measures each ion once. Which statement about the outcomes is correct?
options: Every ion gives the same result: spin up along x.
Roughly half are up along x and half down, even though every ion started identically.
Outcomes alternate strictly between up and down.
Each ion's result is unpredictable, and no measurement orientation could ever make it predictable.
post.explanation: Superposition is basis-relative: in the basis the state is prepared in, the outcome is definite. Randomness only appears when measuring a different basis (e.g. z).
